env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

# A lambda whose body ends in an index, a slice, a parenthesis, a type
# assertion, a composite literal or a string holding closers keeps its
# whole body in the generated function. The module runs natively, ejects,
# and the ejected module builds and runs with go and with go1.27.2 from
# $UPROOT1272 and prints the same output.
cd m
logos run .
stdout '^20 3 20 4 5 30 7 4$'
cp stdout $WORK/native.txt
logos eject -o out
exists out/main.go
cd out
go build ./...
go run .
cmp stdout $WORK/native.txt
exists $UPROOT1272/bin/go
exec $UPROOT1272/bin/go version
stdout '^go version go1\.27\.2 '
exec env -u GOROOT $UPROOT1272/bin/go build -o $WORK/upstream$GOEXE .
exec $WORK/upstream$GOEXE
cmp stdout $WORK/native.txt
cd ..

-- m/go.mod --
module example.com/lambdabody

go 1.27

-- m/main.lgo --
package main

import "fmt"

type P struct{ X, Y int }

func apply(f func(int) int, n int) int {
	return f(n)
}

func main() {
	xs := []int{10, 20, 30}
	a := apply(x => xs[x], 1)
	b := apply(x => (x + 1), 2)
	c := apply(x => xs[1:][x], 0)
	d := apply(x => len(")}//") + x, 0)
	e := apply(x => P{x, 2}.X, 5)
	f := apply(x => xs[x] /* trailing */, 2)
	g := apply(x => any(x).(int), 7) // comment
	h := apply(x => len(`r
)`) + x, 1)
	fmt.Println(a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h)
}
